questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which of these is a valid C source file extension?
questions.explanation: C source files have the .c extension. The compiler compiles these into executable programs.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What does the C compiler do with your source code?
options: Runs it directly line by line
questions.explanation: A C compiler translates your human-readable source code into machine code that the CPU can execute.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which header do you need to use printf() in C?
questions.explanation: stdio.h declares standard input/output functions like printf and scanf.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Every C program must have exactly one function named:
questions.explanation: main() is the entry point the operating system calls to run your program.
The function signature int main() defines the program's entry point.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: printf("Hi")____
questions.explanation: Every C statement ends with a semicolon.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the purpose of return 0; at the end of main() in C?
options: It tells the OS the program finished successfully
questions.answer: It tells the OS the program finished successfully
questions.explanation: Returning 0 from main() signals to the operating system that the program ran without errors.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which of these is a valid variable name in C?
questions.explanation: Variable names must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, digits, and underscores.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which type holds a single character in C?
questions.explanation: char stores a single byte, typically one character.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does this declare? float price = 9.99;
questions.explanation: float declares a decimal number variable, here initialized to 9.99.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: ____ age = 25;
questions.explanation: int is the C keyword for a whole-number variable.
The + operator adds two integers together.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between int and float in C?
options: int is for text, float is for numbers
int is for whole numbers, float is for decimals
float is for whole numbers, int is for decimals
questions.answer: int is for whole numbers, float is for decimals
questions.explanation: int stores integers (e.g. 5, -3), while float stores decimal (floating-point) numbers (e.g. 3.14).

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which symbol is used to open a code block in C?
questions.explanation: Curly braces { } open and close code blocks in C, like after an if statement.
C uses curly braces { } to open a block after an if condition.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which operator checks equality (not assignment) in C?
questions.explanation: == compares two values; = assigns a value.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does != mean in C?
questions.explanation: != is the 'not equal' comparison operator.
i++ increments i by 1 after each loop iteration.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What happens if you write = instead of == inside an if condition in C?
options: It assigns a value instead of comparing — a common bug
questions.answer: It assigns a value instead of comparing — a common bug
questions.explanation: = is assignment, == is comparison. Using = in an if() condition assigns the value and may always be true or false — a tricky bug.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: How many parts does a C for loop header have?
questions.explanation: for (init; condition; update) — three parts separated by semicolons: initialization, condition, and update.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which loop is guaranteed to run its body at least once?
questions.explanation: do { ... } while(condition); checks the condition after running the body.
while(condition) repeats the block as long as the condition is true.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What keyword immediately exits a loop in C?
questions.explanation: break immediately terminates the nearest enclosing loop or switch.
break stops the loop as soon as i equals 5.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between break and continue in a loop?
options: continue exits the loop; break skips to the next iteration
break exits the loop entirely; continue skips to the next iteration
break is for while loops, continue is for for loops
questions.answer: break exits the loop entirely; continue skips to the next iteration
questions.explanation: break stops the loop completely; continue jumps to the top of the loop to begin the next iteration.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What does C++ use instead of printf() to print output?
questions.explanation: C++ uses std::cout (from <iostream>) as its standard way to output text.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which header provides std::cout in C++?
questions.explanation: <iostream> declares the standard input/output stream objects.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: std::cout ____ "Hello, World!";
questions.explanation: The << (insertion) operator sends data into the output stream.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does 'using namespace std;' let you do?
options: Define a new namespace called std
Drop the std:: prefix before names like cout
questions.answer: Drop the std:: prefix before names like cout
questions.explanation: It brings everything in the std namespace into scope, so you can write cout instead of std::cout.
Curly braces open the function body, just like in C.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What does std::endl do when used with std::cout?
options: It inserts a newline and flushes the output stream
It declares the end of a namespace
questions.answer: It inserts a newline and flushes the output stream
questions.explanation: std::endl outputs a newline character '\n' and flushes the buffer, ensuring output appears immediately.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which of these creates an unchangeable value in C++?
questions.explanation: const marks a variable as unmodifiable after initialization.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which keyword declares a constant in C++?
questions.explanation: const marks a variable as unmodifiable after initialization.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: int x = 10;
int& ref = ____;
questions.explanation: int& ref = x; makes ref an alias that refers directly to x.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does the & symbol mean when placed after a type, e.g. int&?
questions.explanation: In C++, & after a type declares a reference variable (an alias to another variable).

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: std::string name = ____Ada Lovelace";
questions.explanation: C++ string literals are wrapped in double quotes.

questions.prompt: RECALL: If you modify a reference variable, what happens to the original?
options: The original is also modified, because they share the same memory
questions.answer: The original is also modified, because they share the same memory
questions.explanation: A reference is an alias — it points to the same memory location, so changes to the reference change the original.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is a function in C++?
options: A reusable block of code that performs a task
A way to store multiple values
questions.answer: A reusable block of code that performs a task
questions.explanation: Functions let you group code under a name so you can call it multiple times without repeating yourself.
return sends the computed value back to the caller.

questions.prompt: SELECT: In 'int add(int a, int b)', what does the first 'int' specify?
options: The return type of the function
questions.answer: The return type of the function
questions.explanation: The type before the function name declares what type of value it returns.

questions.prompt: SELECT: A function declared with return type 'void' means:
questions.explanation: void indicates the function performs an action but returns no value.
A function definition's closing brace needs no trailing semicolon (unlike a declaration).

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between a function declaration and a function definition?
options: A declaration provides the full function body; a definition only names it
A declaration tells the compiler the function exists and its signature; a definition provides the actual body
Declarations are for classes; definitions are for functions
questions.answer: A declaration tells the compiler the function exists and its signature; a definition provides the actual body
questions.explanation: A declaration (prototype) tells the compiler what the function looks like. A definition provides the full implementation.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is a class in C++?
options: A loop that runs a fixed number of times
A built-in data type like int
questions.explanation: A class defines the structure (attributes) and behavior (methods) that objects created from it will have.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which keyword defines a new class in C++?
questions.explanation: class Name { ... }; defines a new class blueprint.
d.bark() calls the bark method on the object d.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does 'public:' control inside a class?
options: Which members are accessible from outside the class
questions.answer: Which members are accessible from outside the class
questions.explanation: Access specifiers like public/private control visibility of members outside the class.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: Dog ____ = Dog();
questions.explanation: This creates an object named myDog of type Dog.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between public and private members in a class?
options: public members can only be accessed inside the class; private ones from anywhere
public members are accessible from outside the class; private ones can only be accessed inside the class
public members are faster; private ones are slower
questions.answer: public members are accessible from outside the class; private ones can only be accessed inside the class
questions.explanation: Encapsulation: public members form the interface of the class, while private members hide internal details.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which of these is a Python source file?
questions.explanation: Python source files have the .py extension.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Python is best described as:
questions.explanation: Python is interpreted (run line by line) and dynamically typed (types are inferred at runtime).

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: ____("Hello, World!")
questions.explanation: print() outputs text to the console in Python.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which symbol starts a comment in Python?
questions.explanation: Everything after # on a line is treated as a comment.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Python uses ____ to define blocks of code instead of curly braces.
questions.explanation: Consistent indentation (spaces) defines code blocks in Python.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: name = ____World"
print(name)
questions.explanation: This string starts with a double quote, so it must also end with one.

questions.prompt: RECALL: Why doesn't Python need semicolons at the end of lines?
options: Each new line is treated as a new statement by default
Python uses brackets to end statements
questions.answer: Each new line is treated as a new statement by default
questions.explanation: In Python, a newline ends a statement, so semicolons are unnecessary (though valid if you want multiple statements on one line).

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which of these is a valid Python variable assignment?
questions.explanation: Python doesn't require a type keyword — just write the variable name, =, and the value.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Do you need to declare a variable's type in Python?
questions.explanation: Python is dynamically typed — you just assign a value and Python infers the type.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: age = 25
name = "Sam"
print(name, ____, age)
questions.explanation: String literals in a print() call must be quoted.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What type is the value produced by 3 / 2 in Python 3?
questions.explanation: The / operator always performs true division and returns a float in Python 3.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: items = ____
items.append("apple")
questions.explanation: Square brackets [] create an empty list in Python.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the result of type(3.14) in Python?
questions.explanation: 3.14 is a decimal literal, so Python infers its type as float. type() returns the class of the value.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What character ends an if statement header in Python?
questions.explanation: In Python, if statements end with a colon, followed by indented code on the next line.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: if score >= 60____
    print("Pass")
else:
    print("Fail")
questions.explanation: Python uses a colon to start a block, followed by an indented line.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which keyword checks another condition after an initial 'if' fails?
questions.explanation: Python's keyword for 'else if' is elif.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does 'and' do between two conditions in Python?
options: True if either condition is true
True only if both conditions are true
questions.answer: True only if both conditions are true
questions.explanation: The 'and' logical operator requires both sides to be true.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: for i in ____(5):
    print(i)
questions.explanation: range(5) generates numbers 0 through 4 for the loop to iterate over.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between 'and', 'or', and 'not' in Python?
options: and = at least one true; or = both true; not = adds
They all mean the same thing
and = addition; or = subtraction; not = multiplication
and = both true; or = at least one true; not = reverses truth value
questions.answer: and = both true; or = at least one true; not = reverses truth value
questions.explanation: 'and' requires both to be True, 'or' needs at least one True, 'not' flips True to False and vice versa.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which keyword starts a function definition in Python?
questions.explanation: def is the keyword used to define a new function in Python.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: ____ greet(name):
    print("Hi", name)
questions.explanation: def defines a new function in Python.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which loop keeps running while a condition stays true?
questions.explanation: while condition: repeats its block as long as the condition is true.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does 'continue' do inside a loop?
questions.explanation: continue skips the rest of the current iteration and moves to the next one.

questions.prompt:

    ____ a + b

print(add(2, 3))
questions.explanation: return sends the result back to wherever the function was called.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What happens if a Python function has no return statement?
questions.explanation: In Python, if a function ends without a return statement, it returns None automatically.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What does JVM stand for in Java?
questions.explanation: The JVM (Java Virtual Machine) is the runtime that executes Java bytecode, making Java programs platform-independent.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is Java's 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' principle?
options: Java code is the same as C++ code
Java programs run on any OS that has a JVM installed
You can only write one Java class per project
questions.answer: Java programs run on any OS that has a JVM installed
questions.explanation: Java compiles to bytecode, which the JVM on any platform can execute — hence 'write once, run anywhere'.
System.out.println() prints text followed by a new line.

questions.prompt: SELECT: In Java, the filename (e.g. Main.java) must match:
options: The name of the main method
The name of its public class
questions.answer: The name of its public class
questions.explanation: Java requires the file name to match the public class it contains.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which method signature is the required entry point of a Java program?
questions.explanation: The JVM looks specifically for this exact main method signature to start the program.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: System.out.println("Hi")____
questions.explanation: Like C and C++, every Java statement ends with a semicolon.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between System.out.print() and System.out.println() in Java?
options: println() adds a newline after the text; print() does not
print() is for numbers; println() is for strings
questions.answer: println() adds a newline after the text; print() does not
questions.explanation: println (print line) appends a newline '\n' after the output, moving the cursor to the next line. print() leaves the cursor on the same line.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Java is a ____ typed language.
questions.explanation: In Java, every variable must have a declared type that is checked at compile time — this is called static typing.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which type holds whole numbers in Java?
questions.explanation: int stores whole (integer) numbers in Java.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: ____ name = "Ada";
questions.explanation: Java's text type is capitalized: String.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What values can a boolean hold in Java?
questions.explanation: boolean is a two-value type: true or false.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: final ____ PI = 3.14;
questions.explanation: double stores decimal numbers; final marks PI as unchangeable.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between int and double in Java?
options: int is for text; double is for numbers
double is for whole numbers; int is for decimals
int holds whole numbers; double holds decimal (floating-point) numbers
questions.answer: int holds whole numbers; double holds decimal (floating-point) numbers
questions.explanation: int cannot store decimals (e.g., 3 not 3.5). double can store large decimal numbers with high precision.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Java uses ____ to group statements in an if block.
questions.explanation: Java uses { } (curly braces) to delimit code blocks, unlike Python which uses indentation.
Java uses curly braces to open a block after an if condition, like C and C++.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which loop is ideal when you know exactly how many times to repeat?
questions.explanation: A for loop's structure (init; condition; update) is built for a known number of iterations.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does the && operator require?
options: At least one condition must be true
questions.explanation: && is Java's logical AND — it requires both sides to be true.
A closing curly brace ends the for loop's block.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the || operator in Java, and when is it true?
options: Logical AND — true only when both sides are true
Logical NOT — reverses a boolean value
Logical OR — true when at least one side is true
Bitwise XOR — true when values differ
questions.answer: Logical OR — true when at least one side is true
questions.explanation: || is Java's logical OR operator. It returns true if either or both conditions are true.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: In Java, a 'method' is:
options: A class that extends another class
A way to store multiple values
A function defined inside a class
questions.answer: A function defined inside a class
questions.explanation: In Java, functions are called 'methods' when they belong to a class.
return sends the computed value back to whatever called the method.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does 'static' mean on a method like main()?
options: It belongs to the class itself, not an object instance
questions.answer: It belongs to the class itself, not an object instance
questions.explanation: static methods belong to the class and can be called without creating an object.

questions.prompt: SELECT: A method with return type 'void' means:
questions.explanation: void means the method performs an action but sends no value back.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: int result = add(2, 3____
questions.explanation: The closing parenthesis matches the opening one from add(2, 3.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is 'method overloading' in Java?
options: Calling the same method too many times
Defining multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists
Inheriting a method from a parent class
questions.answer: Defining multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists
questions.explanation: Overloading allows you to have add(int, int) and add(double, double) — Java picks the right one based on the argument types.
